title: It's Not How Long You Sit — It's How Long Without Getting Up
hook: Same total hours in a chair, different risk. Each extra hour of *unbroken* sitting tracked with a 9% higher risk of dying from cancer; swapping it for light activity, 12% lower.

title: Eating Chili Peppers May Raise the Risk of One Cancer
hook: A major review found heavy chili-pepper eaters had a substantially higher risk of esophageal cancer — though it's an association, not proof, and the picture is murkier for other cancers.

title: Kratom's 6,500% Problem
hook: Sold over the counter as a natural herb, kratom drove 19 U.S. poison center cases in 2010 and more than 1,200 in 2023 — with the severe outcomes climbing too.

title: How to Read a Nutrition Label
hook: The Nutrition Facts label is a cheat sheet hiding in plain sight — learn the few lines that matter and you can size up any packaged food in seconds.

title: COVID Has a Summer Season Too
hook: Every summer since the pandemic began, COVID cases have climbed — and 2026 is no exception. Unlike flu, COVID doesn't wait for winter.

title: Coffee Tracks With a Markedly Healthier Liver
hook: Across 355,000 people followed 13 years, five-plus cups a day came with a 47% lower risk of liver cancer. Decaf worked too — so it isn't the caffeine doing the work.

title: Why Walking Gets Harder With Age
hook: It isn't just weaker muscles. Researchers found older adults stiffen the ankle with every step — buying stability at the cost of efficiency, so each stride does less and costs more.

title: People Past 110 Have an Unusual Immune Arsenal
hook: Supercentenarians carry unusually large numbers of a rare cell type — CD4 T cells that can kill abnormal cells directly, expanded into big clones as if fighting something for decades.

title: Can Diet Help Fight Gum Disease?
hook: A small clinical study found that a low-calorie, fasting-style diet noticeably reduced the inflammation behind gum disease — a hint that what you eat may matter for your gums, not just your brush.

title: Why Aging Muscles Heal More Slowly
hook: A protein that builds up in older muscle stem cells acts like a brake on repair — but the same protein also helps those cells survive the stresses of aging.

title: Neuroscience Is Rediscovering an Idea Freud Had 130 Years Ago
hook: Today's leading theory of the brain describes it as a prediction machine constantly guessing what comes next — an idea a new paper says closely echoes psychoanalysis from over a century ago.

title: An 'Endless' Supply of Cancer-Fighting Immune Cells
hook: A stem-cell-inspired technique lets scientists mass-produce immune cell progenitors that can be engineered to hunt cancer — a step toward off-the-shelf cell therapy.

title: A Mother's Age Shapes Her Offspring — Without Changing Their DNA
hook: The effects of maternal age were assumed to be accumulated DNA damage. In rotifers, they turned out to be reversible switches on gene activity — undone in a single generation.

title: Ultra-Processed Foods: The New Tobacco?
hook: Researchers argue ultra-processed foods echo the tobacco industry's playbook in how they're engineered and marketed — concern crosses party lines, but policy has lagged behind.

title: Cutting Down on Added Sugar
hook: It's not the sugar in an apple that's the problem — it's the added sugar hiding in drinks, sauces, and 'healthy' snacks, adding empty calories you never asked for.

title: COVID Can Wake Up Viruses You Already Had
hook: Most adults carry dormant viruses for life. Researchers found COVID-19 can reactivate them — and one poorly understood viral family tracked strongly with long COVID.

title: Tiny Plastics in Drinking Water May Be Making Bacteria Harder to Kill
hook: Nanoplastics in drinking water don't just pollute — new research suggests they help harmful bacteria build tougher, disinfectant-resistant biofilms inside water systems.

title: Tea Nudged Bone Density Up; Five-Plus Coffees a Day Nudged It Down
hook: Ten years of following nearly 10,000 older women found tea drinkers had slightly denser hips — while more than five cups of coffee a day tracked with lower bone density. Moderate coffee looked fine.

title: One Blood Test for Many Cancers?
hook: A single blood draw that screens for many cancers at once could win FDA approval within months — a potential shift in how cancer gets caught early.

title: Taking Medicines Safely
hook: Medicines help only when used right. Most medication mishaps are preventable with a few habits — reading the label, knowing your list, and asking questions.

title: What Stress Does to Your Body
hook: A jolt of stress is useful — it sharpens you for a real threat. The problem is when the alarm never switches off, and the body pays for staying on high alert.

title: Taking the Stairs Is a Real Workout
hook: In an analysis of more than 480,000 people, regular stair climbers were 39% less likely to die of cardiovascular disease — from a habit that costs nothing and takes no planning.

title: AI Gave Doctors a 'Second Pair of Eyes.' Did Patients Benefit?
hook: A 10,000-visit trial in Kenyan clinics gave clinicians an AI 'second opinion.' It cut their documented errors — but didn't clearly improve how patients actually fared.

title: Understanding Blood Pressure
hook: High blood pressure is called the 'silent killer' for a reason — it usually has no symptoms, yet it quietly raises your risk of heart attack and stroke.

title: Skin Damage Can Begin Before You'd Ever See It
hook: A new light-based imaging technique found that collagen's precise molecular 'handedness' can unravel long before skin looks thinner, weaker, or damaged in any visible way.

title: Preventing STIs
hook: Sexually transmitted infections are common and often symptomless — which is exactly why prevention and testing, not just treatment, are what keep you and your partners healthy.

title: Vitamin C Won't Stop Your Cold
hook: Fifty years after Linus Pauling popularized megadoses, the verdict is in: vitamin C doesn't stop most people catching colds. Taken regularly, it may shorten severe symptoms slightly.

title: Keto Beat Mediterranean and Low-Fat Diets on Liver Fat
hook: All three diets in the trial produced about 10% weight loss — but keto cut liver fat by 67% versus 45%, and about half the keto group no longer met the definition of prediabetes.

title: An Ebola Outbreak That Could Rival the Worst
hook: The 2026 Ebola outbreak in DR Congo has passed 5,000 cases and 2,378 deaths — the fastest fatal spread in Ebola's recorded history, still outpacing the response.

title: Your Gut Bacteria May Be the Reason Vegetables Help Your Heart
hook: Nitrate and plant iron aren't useful on their own. Gut microbes convert them into protective molecules that, in experimental models, tracked with lower blood pressure and better blood sugar.

title: Preventing Falls at Home
hook: Falls are the leading cause of injury for older adults, but most are preventable with a few targeted fixes.

title: Scientists Solved How a Gut Bacterium Triggers Colon Cancer
hook: Researchers cracked a long-standing mystery — how a common gut bacterium's toxin damages the colon and drives cancer — and used that insight to design a decoy protein that blocked it in mice.

title: The First mRNA Flu Vaccine Arrives This Season
hook: Moderna's mRNA flu vaccine — the first flu shot built on the same technology as the COVID vaccines — is now FDA-approved and ready for the coming flu season.

title: Resting Aging Joints Makes Them Worse
hook: The instinct when joints ache is to use them less. That's backwards — cartilage has no blood supply and depends on movement to get fed.

title: Depression May Stall the Making of New Neurons
hook: Adults with depression showed disrupted production of new neurons in the hippocampus — the region that helps keep new experiences from blurring into old painful ones.

title: Surviving Cancer Is Only Half the Battle
hook: More people than ever survive cancer — but the anxiety, depression, and guilt can linger for years after treatment ends, and often go unrecognized.

title: A Protein Switch That Burns Fat and Blocks New Fat Cells
hook: Disabling a protein nicknamed 'Mitch' boosted fat burning and blocked new fat cells from forming in human cells — and made mice leaner and more athletic.

title: Cold, Flu, or COVID?
hook: They share a lot of symptoms, but colds, flu, and COVID-19 differ in how fast they hit and how hard — and telling them apart can change what you do next.

title: Kids With Autism Face a Much Higher Drowning Risk
hook: Children with autism can be up to 160 times more likely than their peers to drown. Florida is now funding swim lessons specifically to close that gap.

title: One Psilocybin Dose, a Month of Brain Change
hook: A single dose of psilocybin left measurable changes in brain activity lasting up to a month — and the people whose brains got more flexible reported more insight and better wellbeing.

title: Can Creatine Help With Depression?
hook: Best known for building muscle, creatine is now being tested against depression — a review of five trials found real benefit in some studies of women, but no effect in others.

title: Blocking a Clumping Enzyme Slowed Alzheimer's in Mice
hook: An ETH Zurich team found the enzyme GRK2 forms clumps in the Alzheimer's brain — and an experimental compound that stopped the clumping kept mice's nerve cells alive longer.

title: Alzheimer's Steals Sleep Through Inflammation, Not Just Plaques
hook: Removing overactive immune cells in the brains of Alzheimer's mice restored more than two hours of sleep a day — even though the amyloid plaques never went away.

title: Stopping Severe Bleeding
hook: Severe bleeding can become life-threatening in minutes. Firm, direct pressure is the single most important thing a bystander can do — and you do it now, not later.

title: Another Daily GLP-1 Pill Posts Double-Digit Weight Loss
hook: Aleniglipron, an experimental once-daily pill, helped people lose up to 12.1% of their body weight in 36 weeks — no injections, no fridge, no meal timing.

title: A Food Compound That May Boost Older Adults' Vaccines
hook: Vaccines protect older adults less well because aging immune systems respond weakly. A small pilot found a compound from wheat germ, mushrooms, and aged cheese helped the weakest responders most.

title: There's a Sleep Sweet Spot for Biological Aging — and It's Narrow
hook: Across 23 different biological aging clocks, the slowest-aging people slept about 6.4 to 7.8 hours a night. Both too little and too much sleep tracked with faster aging.

title: Why Oral Health Matters
hook: Your mouth isn't sealed off from the rest of you. Gum disease and untreated decay are linked to problems well beyond the teeth — and most of it is preventable.

title: Reversing Prediabetes Pays Off for the Heart
hook: Prediabetes isn't a one-way street. People who brought their blood sugar back to normal cut their risk of dying from heart disease or being hospitalized for heart failure by 58%.

title: Cannabis and Stroke: A 37% Signal Across 100 Million People
hook: The largest analysis yet ties recreational drug use to stroke — cocaine nearly doubling risk, amphetamines more than doubling it, and cannabis up 37%, including in young adults.

title: Train for Power, Not Just Strength
hook: Strength is how much force you can produce; power is how fast you can produce it. A few speed-plus-strength moves build the agility that keeps you nimble and injury-free.

title: Seven Habits That Support Fertility
hook: Most fertility advice online is invented. NPR's illustrated guide sticks to what the evidence supports — and notably, half of it applies to the male partner.

title: Dirty Air May Trigger Arthritis Flares
hook: Fine particles from smoke, soot, and dust were linked to worse rheumatoid arthritis and more painful flares — making air quality a possible part of disease management.

title: A Hidden Heart Valve Risk Linked to Gum Disease
hook: Gum disease is already linked to heart disease in general — new research points to a specific mechanism: bacteria that may help trigger a serious, calcium-driven heart valve condition.

title: How Much Exercise You Actually Need
hook: The headline number is smaller than most people fear: about 150 minutes of moderate activity a week — roughly 20-some minutes a day — moves the needle on your health.

title: A HEPA Air Purifier Sharpened Thinking in a Month
hook: Adults over 40 did about 12% better on a test of executive function after one month with a HEPA purifier at home — a hint that the air in your living room is doing something to your brain.

title: The Real Cause of a Common Stroke May Have Been Missed for Decades
hook: A common type of stroke may not be mainly caused by fatty plaque after all — the strongest link was found with damaged small blood vessels deep in the brain.

title: Ozempic Linked to Fewer Bone Fractures
hook: Losing weight often costs you bone. Yet a study of nearly 60,000 people with type 2 diabetes found semaglutide users had about 15% fewer fractures — even though they lost more weight.

title: Counting Teeth Predicted Survival After Cancer Surgery
hook: Among 339 pancreatic cancer patients, those with at least 21 natural teeth lived nearly two years longer after surgery. Teeth are standing in for something bigger.

title: When a Symptom Needs a Doctor
hook: Most everyday symptoms pass on their own. The skill worth having is recognizing the red flags that mean don't wait — call for help now.

title: Three Minutes of Sprinting Rewrote the Blood
hook: Six 30-second sprints shifted nearly a quarter of measured blood proteins and 200-plus metabolites. Ninety minutes of moderate cycling barely moved them.

title: Using Pain Relievers Safely
hook: The pain relievers in your medicine cabinet are safe used right — and surprisingly risky used wrong. Knowing the two main types and their limits is the whole game.

title: Fish Oil Reaches the Brain — But Doesn't Help It
hook: A two-year trial confirmed omega-3s from fish oil pills do reach the brain — but found no real payoff for memory, cognition, or Alzheimer's-related brain changes.

title: What Collagen Supplements Actually Do
hook: The biggest collagen review yet — nearly 8,000 people — found real benefits for skin and arthritic joints with consistent use, but little support for the sports-recovery hype.

title: Brushing and Flossing, Done Right
hook: Brushing twice a day sounds obvious — but for two minutes, with fluoride, and adding daily flossing, is where most people quietly fall short.

title: A Breast Cancer Surge Nobody Can Explain
hook: Breast cancer is climbing fast among Asian American women, and fastest in younger women and aggressive cancers. Better screening doesn't account for it — which means something is still unidentified.

title: A Gel That Could Regrow Tooth Enamel
hook: Enamel is the one part of a tooth your body can't rebuild once it's gone. A new fluoride-free gel aims to change that — coaxing saliva to grow a fresh mineral layer.

title: Keeping Your Brain Healthy
hook: No pill prevents dementia, but the habits that protect your heart turn out to protect your brain too.

title: A Cancer Therapy Put Severe Arthritis Into Remission
hook: Six people with rheumatoid arthritis that had defeated every other treatment got CAR T-cell therapy. Three ended up in remission with no medication at all.

title: Tea Is Good for You — Until You Add the Wrong Things
hook: A major review ties tea to lower risks of heart disease, diabetes, cancer, and cognitive decline — but warns that bottled and bubble teas often pack in ingredients that cancel out the benefits.

title: Hands-Only CPR
hook: If an adult collapses and isn't breathing, you don't need training certificates or rescue breaths — just two steps that can double or triple their chance of survival.

title: Protecting Your Bones
hook: Bone looks permanent, but it's living tissue that thins with age. Osteoporosis weakens it silently until a minor fall causes a major break.

title: Exercise Helps Hip Arthritis Less Than You'd Hope
hook: Exercise therapy is standard advice for hip osteoarthritis. A major review found the average benefit is small — and nobody yet knows which exercises work best.

title: A Drug for 'Undruggable' Pancreatic Cancer
hook: A new drug, daraxonrasib, hits a KRAS mutation long thought 'undruggable' and nearly doubled survival in a trial of advanced pancreatic cancer — a hard-to-treat disease.

title: Protecting Your Hearing
hook: Noise-induced hearing loss is permanent — once those tiny inner-ear cells die, they don't grow back. The good news: it's almost entirely preventable.

title: Midlife Movement Pays Off Decades Later
hook: Exercise and healthy blood sugar in your forties and fifties tracked with slower cognitive decline decades on — and the benefit wasn't the same size for everyone.

title: The Placebo That Worked Even When People Knew
hook: Older adults who knew their pills were fake still improved on memory, fitness, and stress — a hint that the placebo effect doesn't need the lie.

title: Two Measles Deaths, and a Mixed Message from the Top
hook: After two deaths in Pennsylvania's measles outbreak, the U.S. health secretary's response both encouraged vaccination and undercut it — the kind of hedging that costs lives during an outbreak.

title: Building Better Sleep Habits
hook: Good sleep is mostly built in the hours before bed. A handful of simple habits — collectively called sleep hygiene — do more than any gadget.

title: Ultra-Processed Foods Linked to Prostate Cancer Risk
hook: In a nationally representative study of 17,000+ U.S. men, those eating the most ultra-processed food had roughly 24–31% higher prostate cancer risk.

title: Why Regular Checkups Matter
hook: The whole point of a checkup is to catch trouble while it's still quiet — before symptoms show up and while it's easiest to treat.

title: When Sleep Problems Need Help
hook: Better sleep habits fix a lot — but not everything. Loud snoring with gasping, or weeks of being unable to sleep, are signals to see a doctor, not push through.

title: Health Checks Men Skip
hook: Men see doctors less and die younger from preventable causes. A handful of simple checks catch the big risks early.

title: Why Violence Between Dementia Patients Keeps Happening in Care Homes
hook: Nursing homes and assisted living facilities can be fertile ground for violence between residents with dementia — including fatal assaults — and court records show known safeguards keep falling short.

title: Why Sleep Matters
hook: Sleep isn't downtime — it's when your brain consolidates memory and your body repairs itself. Skimp on it for long and the bill comes due in your health.

title: How to Protect Yourself From Ticks
hook: Tick season is here, and a single bite can pass on Lyme and other diseases. A few simple habits sharply cut the risk.

title: Intermittent Fasting's Weight-Loss Edge Held Up a Year Later
hook: A 12-week intermittent fasting program produced weight loss that was still holding a year later — and eating within an early window seemed to help people keep the fat off longest.

title: Protecting Your Eyes
hook: Some of the most serious eye diseases, like glaucoma, steal sight silently with no early symptoms. A regular eye exam is often the only way to catch them in time.

title: Where You Live Could Shape Your Dementia Risk
hook: A massive study of over 214,000 people found dementia risk factors differ widely by country — challenging the idea that one prevention checklist fits everyone.

title: What's Different in the Blood of Centenarians
hook: Some people reach 100 in remarkably good health. A new study finds their blood carries a distinct chemical 'fingerprint' that sets them apart from typical aging.

title: Antibiotics: Use Them Right
hook: Antibiotics are miracle drugs against bacteria — and useless against viruses like colds and flu. Using them when they won't help fuels a genuinely dangerous problem.

title: Postpartum Psychosis Is Rare, Severe, and Treatable
hook: A Boston-area murder trial has put a little-known illness in the spotlight — one psychiatrists say is too often missed until it becomes a crisis.

title: A Spray-On Powder That Stops Bleeding in Seconds
hook: A new spray-on powder can stop life-threatening bleeding in about one second by instantly forming a gel over the wound — even on deep, irregular injuries.

title: Probiotics Rebuilt as Tumor Drug Factories
hook: Engineered probiotic bacteria slipped into pancreatic tumors, switched on cancer-fighting immune cells, and slowed growth in animals — working best alongside standard treatment, not instead of it.

title: When Losing Weight Isn't Enough to Stop Diabetes
hook: Lifestyle change prevents type 2 diabetes for many people — but researchers found one high-risk group whose blood sugar kept climbing even after years of sustained weight loss.

title: A THC Drug Made PTSD Nightmares Disappear for Some
hook: Trauma nightmares are among PTSD's most stubborn symptoms. In a study of a prescription THC medication, more than a third of patients said theirs stopped entirely.

title: A Second-Line Blood Pressure Drug Gets a Second Look
hook: In people with type 2 diabetes, a widely prescribed class of blood pressure drug came with 33% higher risk of serious kidney problems — even in patients already on kidney-protective medicines.

title: The Brain Switch Where Blocking and Activating Both Work
hook: Two obesity drugs do opposite things to the same receptor — and both cause weight loss. Researchers found the answer is location: it depends which part of the brain you hit.

title: How Alzheimer's Might Spread From Cell to Cell
hook: A common brain protein may double as a delivery vehicle for Alzheimer's, ferrying toxic tau out of damaged neurons and into healthy ones — a possible new target for slowing the disease.

title: How Early Stress Leaves a Mark Inside Brain Cells
hook: Early-life stress may physically change how DNA is packaged in the brain, leaving stress genes primed to fire more easily years later. In mice, blocking that repackaging prevented adult anxiety.

title: A Longevity Diet That Helped Mice Eat More and Lose Fat
hook: A modified Mediterranean-style diet, low in protein but with just enough of one amino acid, methionine, helped mice live healthier, leaner lives — and human data hints at a similar link.

title: Cancer Screenings Worth Knowing
hook: Screening looks for cancer before symptoms start — and for a few common cancers, that early catch dramatically improves the odds.

title: Good Fats, Bad Fats
hook: Fat isn't the enemy — the type is what matters. Swapping saturated and trans fats for unsaturated ones beats just trying to eat less fat overall.

title: Losing the Wrong Fat Can Cause Diabetes
hook: We treat body fat as the villain in diabetes. New work shows the opposite failure mode: when healthy fat tissue becomes inflamed and disappears, metabolism collapses too.

title: How Parkinson's Disease Spreads Through the Brain
hook: Yale scientists found two neuron surface proteins that help the toxic protein behind Parkinson's spread from cell to cell — and blocking them dramatically slowed disease progression in mice.

title: Aging Isn't Only Decline
hook: A long-term Yale study found nearly half of adults over 65 actually improved — physically, mentally, or both — and a more positive view of aging tracked with those gains.

title: When 'Getting Older' Is Really Low B12
hook: Fatigue and brain fog get written off as normal aging — but they can be signs of a low vitamin B12 level, a deficiency that's common and fixable.

title: Drinking to Cope With Stress May Permanently Rewire the Brain
hook: Using alcohol to cope with stress at a young age may permanently change the brain — making it harder to adapt to future challenges and raising the risk of drinking again later in life.

title: Weight Loss That Lasts
hook: Crash diets win the first month and lose the year. Slow, steady loss built on habits you can actually keep is what stays off.

title: Exercise Helps the Aging Brain Take Out the Trash
hook: Your brain has a cleaning system that flushes out waste — and it gets sluggish with age. Regular activity appears to support nearly every part of it.

title: Wine, Beer, or Spirits — Does the Drink Matter?
hook: In 340,000 adults tracked for a decade, heavy drinking raised mortality no matter what was in the glass. At lower intakes, wine looked different from beer and spirits.

title: The Silent Spread of Kidney Disease
hook: A global study estimates chronic kidney disease now affects nearly 800 million people — often silently — making it a leading and frequently overlooked cause of death.

title: A Blood Test That Also Says Where the Trouble Is
hook: A UCLA test reads DNA signals in blood to flag several cancers, liver disease, and organ damage — and points to which organ the signal came from.

title: An 8-Hour Eating Window and the Aging Brain
hook: Older women who ate within about 8 to 9 hours a day scored better on planning and problem-solving than those eating across 12 — even though both groups lost the same amount of weight.

title: A Quarter of Recently Deceased NFL Players Had CTE
hook: CTE can only be diagnosed after death, which has made its true prevalence a guess. A new study of former NFL players who died between 2016 and 2021 puts the floor at 25%.

title: The Workout That Burns Fat but Spares Muscle
hook: In adults in their 70s, only high-intensity intervals trimmed body fat while holding onto the muscle that keeps you strong and independent.

title: A 3D-Printed Crown Before You Leave the Chair
hook: Zirconia crowns are strong but slow — up to 100 hours of processing. Researchers cut that to under 30 minutes, which would put a permanent crown inside one appointment.

title: A Common Blood Pressure Drug Could Supercharge a Cancer Therapy
hook: Telmisartan, a widely used blood pressure medication, significantly boosts the cancer drug olaparib — potentially extending its benefits well beyond the BRCA-related tumors it currently treats.

title: Travel Health and Vaccines
hook: Some travel vaccines take weeks to work — and a few diseases abroad have no treatment, only prevention. Planning early is the difference between protected and exposed.

title: A Ten-Cent Heart Drug Makes a Comeback
hook: Digoxin has been treating hearts since the 1700s and costs under ten cents a day. New research suggests low doses cut heart-failure hospitalizations by about 25%.

title: Your Takeaway Order Probably Has More Salt Than It Says
hook: Almost half of takeaway meals tested had more salt than advertised — some serving nearly double the daily limit in one meal. Fish and chips, surprisingly, ranked among the lowest-salt options.

title: The Aging Brain Isn't Sealed Off After All
hook: Stanford researchers found immune cells from the blood streaming into the human brain as early as middle age — overturning the assumption that the brain keeps the body's immune system out.

title: A Cheap Antidepressant May Ease Long COVID's Crushing Fatigue
hook: In a trial of nearly 400 adults, the low-cost antidepressant fluvoxamine significantly reduced long COVID fatigue and improved quality of life — one of the first medications shown to help.

title: Cutting Sweet Foods Didn't Curb the Sweet Tooth
hook: The theory that eating less sweet food retrains your palate just failed a six-month trial: high-, low-, and average-sweetness diets produced no difference in sweet preference.

title: Making Pancreatic Cancer Cells Self-Destruct
hook: Instead of blocking cancer signals, an experimental compound cranks them into overdrive until pancreatic cancer cells destroy themselves — and blocked over 90% of tumor cell migration in lab tests.

title: Your Immune System May Signal How Well a Vaccine Will Work
hook: Analyzing antibody patterns in 4,000+ people, researchers found a state of 'immune readiness' that separated strong vaccine responders from weak ones — before the shot.

title: Exercise Is Better at Keeping Weight Off Than Taking It Off
hook: Exercise is a disappointing weight-loss tool and an excellent weight-maintenance one. Knowing which job it's good at changes how you'd use it.

title: Safe Storage of Medicines and Chemicals
hook: Most poisonings happen at home with everyday products. How you store them is your first line of defense.

title: She Told Only the Chatbot
hook: A 29-year-old confided her suicidal thoughts to an AI chatbot and to no one else — a case that exposes what happens when the most available listener can't call for help.

title: Why GLP-1 Drugs Don't Work for Everyone
hook: Scientists found genetic variants — carried by roughly 1 in 10 people — that seem to cause a kind of 'GLP-1 resistance,' making drugs like Ozempic less effective at controlling blood sugar.

title: Schizophrenia's Missing Connections Have a Map
hook: Brain scans show schizophrenia involves widespread loss of the synapses linking brain cells — and the loss isn't random. It follows the brain's own chemistry and wiring.

title: Caring for a Cold or Flu at Home
hook: Most colds and flu run their course on their own. Good home care is about comfort and rest — and knowing the handful of red flags that mean it's time to get checked.

title: Same BMI, Different Body
hook: Finnish researchers found heavier coffee drinkers carried less fat and more muscle than light drinkers at the same BMI — a reminder that the scale hides a lot.

title: Millions May Be Getting the Wrong Cholesterol Test
hook: A new study finds that apoB — a blood test measuring harmful cholesterol particles directly — beats standard LDL testing at identifying who actually needs more intensive treatment.

title: FDA Approves a Landmark Pancreatic Cancer Drug
hook: U.S. regulators have cleared a first-of-its-kind drug for pancreatic cancer that blocks the protein fueling the vast majority of these tumors — a rare win in the deadliest common cancer.

title: Wildfire Smoke Is Like Smoking Half a Pack a Day
hook: As Canadian wildfire smoke blanketed the U.S. in July 2026, doctors compared short-term exposure to smoking half a pack a day — and a $20 box fan turned out to be a top home defense.

title: Teaching Killer Cells to Survive Inside a Tumor
hook: Natural killer cells are good at destroying cancer and bad at getting into solid tumors. Researchers prepared a tissue-resident version that could do both — and it slowed several tumors in mice.

title: Most 'Avocado Oil' Products Aren't Really Avocado Oil
hook: UC Davis testers bought avocado-oil chips, dressings, and mayo off the shelf — most failed purity testing, cut with cheaper seed oils that cost a fraction of the real thing.

title: A Possible Shortcut Around Calorie Restriction
hook: Moderate calorie restriction lowered an immune protein called C3 that helps drive the slow inflammation of aging — and blocking C3 directly reproduced part of the benefit in mice.

title: Exercise May Ease 'Chemo Brain'
hook: Up to 80% of chemotherapy patients get foggy thinking. In a new trial, a home-based exercise program improved attention and reduced noticeable cognitive problems compared with a placebo.

title: French Fries, Not Potatoes, Tied to Diabetes
hook: A 40-year study of 200,000+ people linked eating french fries about 3 times a week to higher type 2 diabetes risk — while boiled, baked, or mashed potatoes were not.

title: Gut Health: What the Evidence Actually Says
hook: Wellness marketing says your gut is 'broken' and a supplement will fix it. Here's what the evidence really supports — and what's just hype.

title: Heavy Marijuana Smoking and Cancer Risk
hook: Growing research links heavy marijuana smoking to a higher risk of lung and head-and-neck cancers — though scientists still don't know how much use is enough to meaningfully raise that risk.

title: Remote Work's Hidden Cost: Isolation
hook: A new study finds people in fully remote jobs tend to be more socially isolated, anxious, and sad than those who aren't — but researchers say forcing everyone back to the office isn't the fix.

title: APOE2: The Alzheimer's Gene Variant That Protects You
hook: Everyone knows APOE4 raises Alzheimer's risk. Its rare cousin APOE2 does the opposite — and researchers just watched why: those neurons take less DNA damage and repair it faster.

title: Scientists May Have Found How Alzheimer's Kills Brain Cells
hook: Researchers say they've found a previously overlooked mechanism of brain cell death behind both Alzheimer's and frontotemporal dementia — and it might be possible to interrupt.

title: An AI Search Through the Genome Turned Up a Natural Appetite Peptide
hook: Stanford scientists let an algorithm read all 20,000 human protein-coding genes looking for hidden hormones. It found a 12-amino-acid peptide that curbs appetite through the hypothalamus alone.

title: Do Calcium and Vitamin D Pills Really Protect Bones?
hook: Calcium and vitamin D pills are almost automatic for aging bones. But a review of nearly 154,000 people found that for most older adults, they barely move the needle on fractures or falls.

title: Cannabis for Stress May Disrupt the Stress System
hook: Frequent cannabis users woke up with cortisol already elevated — raising the possibility that using it to relax gradually dysregulates the system that handles stress.

title: A Common Pesticide Linked to Parkinson's
hook: People living near where the pesticide chlorpyrifos was used were more than twice as likely to develop Parkinson's disease, a UCLA study found.

title: Quick Ways to Calm Down
hook: When stress spikes, you can't think your way calm — but you can breathe your way there. A few simple tools work in minutes, anywhere.

title: AI Calorie Apps Missed 250–345 Calories per Meal
hook: Snap a photo, get a number — and NIH researchers found that number runs 250 to 345 calories light per meal, with about 30 grams of fat simply unaccounted for.

title: Dry Eye Is a Menopause Symptom Almost Nobody Warns You About
hook: Around half of women in the menopausal transition have dry eye symptoms, and the rate in women over 50 is double that of men. The culprit is usually oil glands in the eyelids, not a shortage of tears.

title: Losing Just 80 Minutes of Sleep a Night Could Make You Gain Weight
hook: You don't need a dramatic all-nighter to feel the metabolic cost of short sleep. Losing about 80 minutes a night for six weeks was enough to cause weight gain and less activity in a new study.

title: Becoming a Dad Changes the Brain
hook: New-baby brain rewiring isn't just a mother's story: recent research finds fathers' brains change too — and a survey of thousands of dads found most embracing the caregiver role.

title: Building Everyday Resilience
hook: Resilience isn't a personality you're born with — it's a set of habits and connections you can build, the way you build a muscle.

title: A New Weight-Loss Pill Beats Oral Ozempic in a Major Trial
hook: Orforglipron, a once-daily weight-loss pill, outperformed oral semaglutide on weight loss and blood sugar in a major trial — and skips the refrigeration and meal-timing rules.

title: TIPP: Four Skills for When You're Too Distressed to Think
hook: When emotion is so intense you can't reason your way calm, a clinical psychologist's go-to is TIPP — four body-based moves that lower the intensity fast enough to think again.

title: Prostate Health and Screening
hook: PSA screening for prostate cancer isn't an automatic yes. It's a genuine judgment call you make with your doctor.

title: An Appetite Hormone With a Second Job in the Liver
hook: GDF15 is known for suppressing appetite. McMaster researchers found it also runs a brain-to-liver circuit that calms liver inflammation — even without any weight loss.

title: The Case Against Full-Fat Dairy Keeps Weakening
hook: Adults eating three servings of full-fat dairy a day for 12 weeks saw no rise in weight, body fat, cholesterol, or insulin resistance — and their blood pressure improved.

title: Loneliness Is a Health Risk
hook: Chronic loneliness isn't just a bad feeling — it's linked to higher risk of heart disease, depression, and early death. And it's far more common than people admit.

title: An AI-Designed 'Universal' Coronavirus Vaccine
hook: A vaccine designed with AI to target a whole virus family — not one strain — passed its first human trial safely and triggered immunity against SARS-CoV-2, SARS, and pandemic-risk bat viruses.

title: The Strength-Training Sweet Spot for a Longer Life
hook: A 30-year study of 147,000 people points to a modest target: about 90–120 minutes of strength training a week was linked to the biggest drop in risk of dying.

title: Why Low-Carb Sends Some People's Cholesterol Soaring
hook: The same low-carb diet can leave one person's LDL untouched and send another's climbing — and genetic predisposition to high cholesterol, plus saturated fat intake, tracks the difference.

title: Fish, Rice, and a Clever Way to Fight Parasitic Worms
hook: Farmers in Senegal are adding fish to their rice paddies — and the fish do triple duty: fertilizing the crop, feeding the family, and eating the snails that spread a dangerous parasitic worm.

title: Why the Sober Stretch Can Set Up the Relapse
hook: Mice that turned compulsive after a period of alcohol abstinence showed double the activity in a stress-and-addiction brain region — and the signal appeared before they drank.

title: The Menstrual Cycle, Explained
hook: Your cycle is a monthly report card on your health. Knowing what's normal makes the rare red flag easy to spot.

title: Your Brain Fights to Get the Weight Back
hook: Regaining weight isn't a willpower failure. The brain treats your former higher weight as normal and defends it — with more hunger, stronger cravings, and less energy burned.

title: Too Busy to Notice You're Busy? Do a Time Audit
hook: Most of us can't say where our hours actually go. Writing them down for a few days is a blunt, effective way to find out — and to reclaim some.

title: The Colon Cancer Warning Signs Young Adults Shrug Off
hook: Colorectal cancer is now the leading cause of cancer death in people under 50 — and it's still rising. A handful of symptoms are worth taking seriously long before the recommended screening age.

title: Three Drugs Together Cleared HIV Where None Could Alone
hook: In newborn primates treated within three days of exposure, a one-time combination of three therapies completely cleared the virus — something none of the three achieved on its own.

title: How Extreme Heat Harms the Body
hook: Your body cools itself by sweating — but in high heat and humidity, that system can be overwhelmed, and the result can be deadly. Knowing the signs is how you stay ahead of it.

title: A Vaccine for One of the World's Biggest Child Killers
hook: Diarrheal disease kills over a million people a year, nearly half of them children under five. A vaccine against shigella — a leading cause — is now in trials.

title: The Shingles Shot and Dementia Risk
hook: In more than 500,000 older adults, those who got Shingrix were 24% less likely to be diagnosed with dementia over four years — an unusually large signal from a vaccine you're already due for.

title: Hormone Therapy for Menopause: Wonder Drug or Not?
hook: Doctors spent years warning women off hormone therapy. Now the internet calls it a miracle. The honest answer sits in between — and depends on who you are.

title: Omega-3 and Aspirin Matched Antibiotics for Gum Disease
hook: In a year-long study of severe gum disease, omega-3 plus low-dose aspirin hit the treatment goal about as often as antibiotics did — roughly 58% either way.

title: Understanding Cholesterol
hook: Cholesterol has a good side and a bad side. Too much of the bad kind builds up in your arteries for years — silently — until it triggers a heart attack or stroke.

title: A Sugar-Coated Therapy Boosted Brain Cancer Survival by 50% in Mice
hook: An experimental nanoparticle therapy snuck past glioblastoma's toughest defense — the blood-brain barrier — and boosted median survival by 50% in mice, without harming other organs.

title: You Probably Need More Protein Than the Minimum
hook: The official protein guideline is a floor set to prevent deficiency — not the amount that keeps you strong. A new review argues most people, especially with age, do better with more.

title: Teen Cannabis Use and the Slowing of Thinking Skills
hook: Teens who started using cannabis kept developing normally at first — then their memory, attention, and processing speed leveled off while non-users kept improving.

title: The Campus Drug Problem Is Still Alcohol
hook: A cocaine bust makes the news; the drug actually harming college students doesn't. Cocaine use among young adults is down — heavy drinking is what the research keeps pointing at.

title: Building Healthier Screen Habits
hook: You don't need to quit your phone — just out-design it. A few small tweaks beat willpower for taking back your attention.

title: Easing Knee Arthritis Without Surgery
hook: Knee osteoarthritis often ends in joint replacement. A minimally invasive procedure that blocks the inflammation-feeding blood vessels eased pain for at least a year — no surgery.

title: Popular Sugar Substitutes Linked to Faster Brain Aging
hook: Adults who consumed the most artificial sweeteners showed cognitive decline roughly 1.6 years faster than those who consumed the least — especially people under 60 or with diabetes.

title: When the Sun Isn't Enough for Vitamin D
hook: We're told a little summer sun tops up your vitamin D. A study found that for older adults and people with darker skin, the sun barely moved the needle.

title: Where Your Nitrate Comes From May Shape Dementia Risk
hook: A 54,000-person study suggests the source of dietary nitrate matters more than the amount: from vegetables it tracked with lower dementia risk; from red meat and drinking water, higher.

title: Intermittent Fasting vs. Counting Calories
hook: A new study found intermittent fasting produced as much weight loss as strict calorie counting — without the constant feeling of monitoring every bite.

title: Alcohol and Your Health
hook: There's no amount of alcohol proven to be good for you — but there's a meaningful difference between a glass with dinner and patterns that quietly raise your risk of cancer, liver disease, and more.

title: A Nightly Pill Cut Sleep Apnea Events by 44% in a Phase 3 Trial
hook: CPAP works — for the people who can tolerate it. AD109, a once-nightly pill that strengthens the muscles holding the airway open, cut breathing interruptions by about 44% in a major trial.

title: Do Humans Have Hidden Regenerative Powers?
hook: Salamanders regrow lost limbs; mammals just scar over. New work hints our regenerative ability isn't gone — only switched off — and that it might be switched back on.

title: Coffee May Help Your Heart — Energy Drinks, Not So Much
hook: A new American Heart Association review says up to ~400 mg of caffeine a day is fine for most hearts, and coffee may even lower some risks. The catch is what you get it from.

title: AI Turned 672 Antibodies Into Ones That Work Inside Cells
hook: Ordinary antibodies fall apart inside a cell. An Essex team used AI protein design to fix that — opening a door on the tangled proteins behind Alzheimer's, Parkinson's and MND.

title: Fiber's Byproduct Seems to Leave the Gut a Memory
hook: Butyrate — what gut bacteria make from dietary fiber — doesn't just calm inflammation while it's present. It appears to reprogram the gut lining to keep calming it afterwards.

title: Why Fructose Doesn't Fill You Up
hook: In mice, glucose switched off hunger signals but fructose barely did — a hint that the kind of sugar, not just the calories, shapes appetite.

title: Recognizing Depression and Anxiety
hook: Depression and anxiety are among the most common — and most treatable — health conditions. Knowing the signs is the first step to getting help that works.

title: Sugar Before Age 2, Health at Age 70
hook: Britain's postwar sugar rationing ended abruptly in 1953, creating a natural experiment. Babies who got less sugar early had lower cancer rates decades later.

title: The Color Missing From Your Indoor Lighting
hook: Indigo light is abundant in sunlight and largely absent from indoor LEDs. In tree shrews, adding it back completely prevented nearsightedness.

title: Cialis as a Longevity Drug? What the Evidence Actually Says
hook: Online clinics and podcasters are selling tadalafil as an all-purpose longevity pill. The studies behind the hype are real — and every one of them is the kind that can't prove cause.

title: A Wearable Patch That Nudges You Into REM Sleep
hook: A wearable ultrasound patch got 28 people into REM sleep 43 minutes sooner and kept them there about 16 minutes longer — no drugs, no surgery.

title: Fifteen Years of Produce Safety Rules, and Outbreaks Keep Coming
hook: The FDA wrote real rules for how farms grow your salad. The problem is almost nobody checks whether farms follow them — some have never had a single inspection.

title: Four Exercises for When You Can't Stop Picking Yourself Apart
hook: Psychologist Diana Hill's approach to appearance obsession doesn't argue with the thought — it changes your relationship to it, so it stops running the day.

title: Micro-Awakenings May Be an Early Alzheimer's Signal
hook: Healthy middle-aged adults with more frequent micro-awakenings during sleep carried higher genetic risk for Alzheimer's — years before any memory symptoms appeared.

title: GLP-1 Drugs Linked to Lower Breast Cancer Risk
hook: A large study found women on GLP-1 drugs were about 30% less likely to develop breast cancer — a promising association, not yet proof, with trials now being planned to test it.

title: Flu and Seasonal Shots
hook: Some vaccines are a yearly habit, not a one-time event — because the viruses change, or immunity fades, and a fresh shot keeps protection current each season.

title: Speaking Four Languages, With a Brain 13 Years Younger
hook: People fluent in four languages had brains that looked about 13 years younger than monolinguals'. Starting early and reaching real fluency both strengthened the effect.

title: GLP-1 Drugs Carry a Small but Real Hair-Loss Signal
hook: Anecdotes about thinning hair on Ozempic and Mounjaro now have data behind them: a BMJ study found a higher rate of hair loss than with two other diabetes drug classes. The good news is which kind.

title: Food Safety at Home
hook: Most food poisoning starts in an ordinary kitchen. Four simple habits — clean, separate, cook, chill — prevent the great majority of it.

title: SuperAgers' Memories Are Extraordinary. Their Genes Are Not.
hook: People in their 80s with the memory of a 50-year-old were expected to have lucky DNA. They don't — their Alzheimer's risk genes look like everyone else's, which points the search back at life itself.

title: A Twice-a-Year Shot to Prevent HIV
hook: South Africa is rolling out lenacapavir — an HIV-prevention injection given just twice a year — a potential game-changer for a country at the center of the epidemic, if doses and funding hold up.

title: The Link Between Diabetes and Dementia
hook: Diabetes and dementia keep turning up together — and it may be no coincidence. Trouble with insulin and blood sugar can starve, inflame, and damage the brain's blood vessels.

title: Melanoma's Secret to Cheating Death
hook: Scientists say they've found the missing genetic ingredient that lets melanoma cells become effectively immortal — a discovery that could open new lines of attack on the cancer.

title: That Ringing in Your Ears Can Be an Early Warning
hook: Hearing loss rarely arrives as silence. It often shows up first as ringing in the ears or a struggle to follow conversation in a noisy room — signs worth heeding early.

title: Museums, Movies, and Theater May Help Your Body Stay Younger
hook: Older adults who regularly go to museums, movies, or concerts tended to have bodies that functioned like people about three years younger — entertainment with a possible health dividend.

title: Rescuing an Antibiotic Superbugs Had Beaten
hook: Rather than invent a new antibiotic, scientists paired an old one with a small 'helper' molecule that disables the bug's resistance — reviving a drug that resistant bacteria had shrugged off.

title: Nearly Half of Kidney Transplant Candidates Never Get Started
hook: A massive national study found that nearly half of Americans referred for a kidney transplant never even begin the evaluation — and where you live can matter as much as your health.

title: Staying Strong as You Age
hook: The decline we associate with old age is partly the result of doing less. Staying active — in four distinct ways — keeps you independent far longer.

title: This Tick Can Give You a Meat Allergy
hook: The lone star tick is spreading across much of the U.S. — and its bite can trigger alpha-gal syndrome, a delayed allergic reaction to red meat.

title: The Molecular Switch Behind Exercise's Anti-Aging Effect on Muscle
hook: Researchers found a molecular switch that helps explain why exercise keeps aging muscles healthy: it lowers a gene called DEAF1, letting older muscle clear out damage and repair itself.

title: Know Your Numbers
hook: A handful of routine numbers — blood pressure, cholesterol, blood sugar, and waist size — quietly predict much of your future health, and most have no symptoms until something breaks.

title: Childhood Sugary Drinks and Blood Pressure Decades Later
hook: A 25-year study followed kids into adulthood and found a daily soda, sports drink, or juice habit tracked with higher blood pressure years later — and one simple swap moved the needle.

title: What Is an Aortic Dissection?
hook: A tear in the wall of the body's largest artery — the emergency behind Sen. Lindsey Graham's death — can go from first symptom to fatal in minutes. Here's what it is and why speed matters.

title: A Surprising Link Between SSRIs and Heart Valve Disease
hook: Serotonin — the mood chemical targeted by SSRI antidepressants — may also speed up a common heart valve disease in people who carry a specific genetic variant, new research finds.

title: Quitting Smoking
hook: Your body starts repairing itself within hours of your last cigarette. Quitting is hard and relapse is common — but the right support roughly doubles your odds of success.

title: Screens and Your Wellbeing
hook: It's not just how many hours you're on a screen — it's how and when. The same phone can leave you rested or wrecked depending on use.

title: Getting Help for Mental Health
hook: Mental health treatment works for most people — and the hardest part is usually just starting. Here's how to take the first step.

title: Tumors That Recruit Your Own Nerves
hook: Triple-negative breast tumors appear to hijack healing immune cells and use them to wire nerves into themselves — a nerve supply that may help the cancer grow and resist treatment.

title: A Popular Joint Supplement Is Linked to Faster Dementia
hook: A large study tied glucosamine — a popular joint supplement — to a 25% higher chance of dementia and a faster slide to Alzheimer's. It's an association, not proof.

title: The Stool Test You Mail Back Cuts Death Risk by 43%
hook: Across 376,000 Swedes followed long-term, people who took part in colorectal cancer screening were 43% less likely to die of it. The test is one you do at home.

title: How the Biggest Alzheimer's Risk Gene May Start Early
hook: In mice, APOE4 raised a protein called Nell2, shrinking neurons and leaving memory circuits oddly overactive years before memory failed — and lowering Nell2 reversed it.

title: An Injection That Regenerates Arthritic Joints
hook: In animal studies, a single injection restored arthritic joints to health within weeks — by regenerating damaged tissue rather than just easing the pain.

title: Why a Damaged Liver May Not Bounce Back After You Stop Drinking
hook: The liver is famously good at rebuilding itself — but in alcohol-related liver disease, damaged cells can get stuck in a regenerative limbo that quitting alone doesn't release.

title: Ozempic and Wegovy May Slow Biological Aging
hook: Semaglutide, the drug behind Ozempic and Wegovy, slowed biological aging markers in a study of adults with HIV — the first clinical evidence it may affect aging itself, not just weight or blood sugar.

title: Belly Fat Plus Low Vitamin D Is Worse Than Either Alone
hook: In 5,500+ adults over 50, having both abdominal obesity and vitamin D deficiency was linked to a 123% higher risk of death over six years — more than either risk factor by itself.

title: Smoke and Carbon Monoxide Alarms
hook: Carbon monoxide is invisible and odorless. A working alarm is the only thing that will warn you before it's too late.

title: GLP-1 Drugs Linked to Lower Addiction Risk
hook: A study of ~600,000 U.S. veterans links GLP-1 drugs like semaglutide to lower rates of addiction and overdose — an association, not proof that the drugs cause the effect.

title: The First New Sunscreen Filter in the U.S. in 20 Years
hook: The FDA approved bemotrizinol — a broad-spectrum UV filter used for decades in Europe and Asia — the first new sunscreen ingredient cleared in the U.S. in about 20 years.

title: A Spinal-Injury Drug Repairs DNA Damage in Alzheimer's
hook: A drug originally developed for spinal cord injury repaired DNA damage and cut brain inflammation in mouse Alzheimer's studies — and it's already cleared a human safety trial.

title: Fast Walkers in Their 80s Have Sharper Minds
hook: A study of people 80 and older found the fastest walkers had about half the risk of cognitive decline — one more sign that a strong stride and a strong brain go together.

title: Handwashing: The Cheapest Medicine
hook: It sounds almost too simple, but washing your hands well is one of the most effective things you can do to stop the spread of illness in a household.

title: The Mysterious 'Hum' Heard Around the World May Be Explained
hook: For decades, people worldwide have reported hearing a mysterious low hum with no external source. New research points to an internal explanation: low-frequency tinnitus that only feels external.

title: An Experimental Vaccine Against Fentanyl Overdose
hook: Scripps researchers are testing a vaccine that trains the immune system to grab fentanyl in the bloodstream before it reaches the brain — and to recognize a broad range of its deadliest variants.

title: With Federal Guidance Frozen, Medical Groups Issued Their Own Vaccine Advice
hook: Four major physician groups issued their own COVID, flu and RSV recommendations to fill the void left by the CDC's frozen process — and they advise the shots more broadly than federal guidance.

title: Psilocybin Outside the Lab
hook: Oregon legalized supervised psilocybin without requiring a diagnosis. The first real-world data from thousands of sessions looks promising — and it isn't a clinical trial.

title: Common Preservatives, Higher Heart Risk
hook: Tracking 112,000 people for up to eight years, researchers linked diets high in certain common food preservatives to more high blood pressure, heart attacks, and strokes.

title: A Tape Measure Around Your Waist Beats the BMI You've Been Using
hook: BMI missed many people who actually had obesity. A plain waist measurement caught unhealthy body fat nearly as well as far more complicated methods — and it costs nothing.

title: Preventing Type 2 Diabetes
hook: Type 2 diabetes often arrives slowly, with a warning stage called prediabetes — and at that stage, modest lifestyle changes can stop or delay it.

title: Why Connection Matters
hook: Strong relationships aren't just nice to have — they predict how long and how well you live, on par with diet and exercise.

title: A Record Summer for Foodborne Illness
hook: Cyclosporiasis cases topped 10,000 and the CDC traced a fresh salmonella outbreak to imported jalapeños. Heat plus tainted produce made 2026 a record year.

title: Understanding Addiction
hook: Addiction isn't a lack of willpower or a moral failing — it's a treatable medical condition that changes how the brain works. And like other chronic illnesses, it responds to treatment.

title: Heat Kills About Five Times More Americans Than the Official Count Says
hook: Federal records list roughly 1,700 U.S. heat deaths a year. A two-year NPR and Boston University investigation modeled the real figure at around 9,000 — and found the risk isn't limited to hot states.

title: Spotting and Beating Burnout
hook: Burnout isn't just being tired — it's exhaustion, cynicism, and feeling ineffective, and it comes from chronic stress you haven't been able to offload.

title: A Constipation Drug May Help Clear Depression's Brain Fog
hook: An existing constipation drug may double as a treatment for the mental fog that lingers after depression — in a small trial, a week of it improved memory, attention, and thinking speed.

title: Drug Checking Strips Lose Federal Funding
hook: Test strips let someone check street drugs for hidden fentanyl before using. Federal officials say grant money can no longer buy them — and overdose workers are alarmed.

title: Meta Agrees to Shut Teens Out at Night and During School
hook: Researchers have argued for years that the worst social media harm is what it displaces — sleep and school. Meta has now agreed to cut minors off during exactly those hours.

title: A Gut Bacterium Linked to Holding On to Your Strength
hook: Older adults carrying Roseburia inulinivorans had 29% stronger handgrip. Give it to mice and they gained about 30% grip strength and built more fast-twitch fiber.

title: Ozempic May Work Backwards From What Scientists Expected
hook: The obvious guess was that semaglutide switches off the brain's hunger neurons. In mice it appears to switch them on — and that activation seems necessary to keep the fat off.

title: Why Testosterone Is Suddenly Everywhere
hook: Testosterone is having a moment — the military will screen service members for low levels, and the Trump administration wants to expand access. Worth a look before the marketing reaches you.

title: How to Think About a Summer of Food Recalls
hook: A record run of recalls doesn't mean food got dramatically more dangerous — it mostly means detection got better. What matters is what's in your fridge right now.

title: The 'Dark Matter' Hiding in Your Food
hook: A nutrition label lists a few dozen things; your food holds thousands. Scientists call the rest 'nutritional dark matter' — and it may shape disease, aging, and why diets affect people so differently.

title: Nearly Half of Dementia Risk Is Something You Can Change
hook: A long-term brain study tied smoking, high blood pressure, heart disease, and high blood lipids to the damage behind vascular dementia — risks that are all treatable.

title: ADHD Looks Different in Women — and Gets Missed for Decades
hook: Girls with ADHD look distracted rather than disruptive, so diagnosis often waits until adulthood. The cost isn't just lost years — one UK study found women with ADHD die nearly nine years earlier.

title: FDA Scientists Flag Concerns With Trendy Peptides
hook: Peptides marketed for muscle gain, weight loss, and anti-aging are booming — but FDA scientists found little proof they work or are safe. Compounding pharmacies now want to make them legally.

title: Teen Cannabis Use and Serious Mental Illness
hook: A study of more than 463,000 adolescents tied teen cannabis use to roughly double the risk of serious mental illness — and the use usually came first.

title: Ozempic May Have Revealed the Brain's Craving Switch
hook: GLP-1 drugs blunt more than hunger — they dull cravings for alcohol too. Scientists are tracing that effect to one small brain region: the lateral septum.

title: A Surprising Link Between Vitamin C and Brain Health
hook: In a study of over 2,000 older adults, people with lower blood vitamin C had less gray matter and weaker brain connections tied to memory and attention.

title: Is 150 Minutes a Week Really Enough?
hook: The famous 150-minute target may buy less heart protection than advertised. A large study points to roughly 560–610 minutes a week for substantially bigger gains.

title: An Experimental Pill That Stopped a Measles-Like Virus From Spreading
hook: A drug called GHP-88310 blocked airborne spread of a measles-like virus in ferrets — the first time a polymerase inhibitor has done that. It could one day shut outbreaks down, not replace vaccines.

title: Helping Someone Who Is Choking
hook: If someone can still cough or speak, let them cough. If they can't breathe, speak, or cough, that's the moment to act — and to get help on the way.

title: Mindfulness Training May Move Your Blood Pressure in Eight Weeks
hook: Programs that train mindfulness, gratitude, and optimism improved blood pressure and inflammation markers within 8 to 12 weeks — with daily practice plus regular reinforcement doing the heavy lifting.

title: What Mental Health Really Means
hook: Mental health isn't just the absence of illness — it's being able to cope with life's stresses, work, learn, and contribute. Everyone has it, and it can be cared for.

title: Run Low on Fiber and Your Gut Bugs Start Eating You
hook: Gut microbes have to eat something. When fiber runs short, researchers found, they turn on the protein-rich mucus layer that lines and protects your gut.

title: Why Middle Age Is Getting Harder in the U.S.
hook: A new international study finds middle-aged Americans are lonelier, more depressed, and in worse health than earlier generations — with financial strain and fraying social ties at the root.

title: Medicare's $50 Obesity Drug Program Is Catching On
hook: A federal program that started July 1 puts some obesity drugs at $50 a month for eligible Medicare beneficiaries — and pharmacies say demand is already large.

title: Immune Cells May Remember Obesity for Years After the Weight Comes Off
hook: Losing weight moves the number on the scale quickly. Researchers found a molecular imprint in key immune cells that may persist for 5 to 10 years afterward — one reason some risks fade slowly.

title: Menopause: What to Expect
hook: Menopause isn't a sudden switch. It's a years-long transition with real symptoms and real options to manage them.

title: Scientists Tested 39 Sweeteners and Found Unexpected Gut Effects
hook: A big lab study found common sweeteners can quietly reshape gut bacteria — and interact with medications and caffeine in more than 100 unexpected ways.

title: Maybe Plaques Aren't the Whole Story
hook: New research suggests Alzheimer's may start not with plaques themselves, but with amyloid beta interfering with tau — the protein that keeps neurons running.

title: Vaccines Adults Still Need
hook: Vaccination isn't just a childhood checklist. Protection from some shots fades, new ones are recommended with age, and a few need regular boosters.

title: When Scrolling Stops Being a Habit
hook: Losing sleep to your phone isn't automatically an addiction — but there's a line, and courts are now arguing over who put it there.

title: People on GLP-1 Drugs May Start Moving Less
hook: Weight-loss drugs like Ozempic clearly shrink the number on the scale — but Fitbit data suggests users also take fewer steps, raising a flag about losing muscle along with fat.

title: The Thymus: A 'Forgotten' Organ Tied to Longevity
hook: The thymus was thought to clock out after childhood. A large imaging study found adults with healthier-looking thymuses tended to live longer — a striking link, not a prescription.

title: The Inherited Heart Risk a Standard Cholesterol Test Misses
hook: About 1 in 5 people carry high Lp(a) — an inherited cholesterol particle tied to stroke and cardiac death that routine lipid panels don't measure. One blood test finds it.

title: Most Women With "Recurrent UTIs" May Not Have a Bladder Problem at All
hook: In a review of 253 women diagnosed with recurrent UTIs, only 15% had a problem confined to the bladder or urinary tract. The rest had hormonally driven vulvar inflammation or a tight pelvic floor.

title: A Record Cyclospora Outbreak With an Elusive Source
hook: A Cyclospora outbreak has now topped 4,100 cases — a U.S. record — even after the FDA retracted its lone positive lab test, leaving Taylor Farms lettuce as the prime suspect on epidemiology alone.

title: The Heart Nutrient You Might Be Missing
hook: Hitting your five-a-day may not be enough: researchers say foods rich in flavanols — berries, apples, beans, tea — are a separate lever for heart health most diets miss.

title: Raw Milk Sickened More Than 100 People in Idaho
hook: While cyclospora took the headlines, unpasteurized milk quietly sent an Idaho outbreak past 100 cases — a reminder of what pasteurization is actually for.

title: Ultra-Processed Foods May Dull Your Focus
hook: In 2,100 adults, eating more ultra-processed food tracked with poorer attention and slower thinking — even among people whose diets were otherwise healthy.

title: Your Backyard Bird Feeder Could Be a Bird Flu Hotspot
hook: A feeder does something nature rarely does: it crowds species that wouldn't normally mix into one small spot. During an H5N1 outbreak, that's exactly how a virus spreads.

title: Common Medications May Reshape Your Gut for Years After the Last Dose
hook: It's not just antibiotics. In more than 2,500 people, antidepressants, beta-blockers, acid reducers, and benzodiazepines all left microbial fingerprints — some still detectable years later.

title: Move More, Sit Less
hook: Even if you hit the gym, hours of unbroken sitting carry their own health risk. Breaking up the day with movement matters as much as the workout.

title: The 'Foamy' Brain Cells Linked to Aggressive MS
hook: Why does multiple sclerosis race ahead in some people and stay quiet in others? Brain tissue from severe cases reveals fat-stuffed immune cells that may flip from repair mode to relentless damage.

title: "Broken Heart Syndrome" Looks Exactly Like a Heart Attack
hook: Sudden grief or shock can stun the heart muscle badly enough to mimic a heart attack — same chest pain, same ECG changes. A new blood-based score may tell them apart without threading a catheter.

title: An Ultrasound Treatment That May Stop Arthritis Before It Starts
hook: A simple, non-invasive ultrasound treatment nudges immune cells in an injured joint away from damaging inflammation and toward repair — potentially heading off arthritis before it takes hold.

title: An mRNA Vaccine Aimed at Keeping Melanoma From Coming Back
hook: Merck and Moderna say a late-stage trial of their mRNA melanoma vaccine succeeded — a shot meant not to prevent cancer, but to stop it from returning after surgery.

title: Estrogen Therapy Linked to Fewer Alzheimer's Changes in the Brain
hook: In a study of more than 21,000 women, those who used estrogen-only hormone therapy later in life had 39% lower odds of a dementia diagnosis — and cleaner-looking brains at autopsy.

title: Why Strength Training Matters
hook: Cardio gets the glory, but lifting, resistance bands, and bodyweight moves protect something running can't: the muscle and bone you'll rely on for decades.

title: Brain Scans Suggest Two Types of Autism
hook: Brain-scan research suggests autism may include at least two biologically distinct subtypes — one with more brain 'chatter,' one with less — though this is early science, not a clinical test.

title: A Calculator for Statin Side-Effect Worry
hook: A new Oxford calculator predicts your personal risk of serious statin muscle problems — and finds over 98% of eligible people are actually at low risk.

title: The Largest Opioid Review Yet: Often No Better Than Placebo
hook: The biggest review yet of opioids for short-term pain found their benefits are often small and brief — and for some surgeries and kidney stones, no better than a placebo.

title: Your Brain Wasn't Built for This Much Bad News
hook: We're wired to watch for danger — useful when threats were local. A nonstop feed of global bad news hijacks that instinct, and the fix isn't tuning out but changing how you tune in.

title: Treating Minor Cuts and Burns
hook: Most household cuts and burns heal fine with the right first move — and knowing the few that need a doctor keeps a small injury from becoming a big one.

title: Building a Balanced Plate
hook: Forget counting every calorie — the simplest healthy-eating tool is a picture of a plate: half produce, a quarter grains, a quarter protein.

title: A Kidney Drug May Help Millions More
hook: Three major studies found finerenone protects the kidneys and heart in far more people than thought — including those with non-diabetic kidney disease, a group with few good options.

title: A $70 Billion Industry With Thin Evidence
hook: Supplements are one of the fastest-growing corners of health spending. For most of what's on the shelf, there's little evidence it does what the label implies.

title: A Low-Fat Vegan Diet Cut Calories Without Cutting Food
hook: In a 16-week trial, people eating mostly plants took in about 357 fewer calories a day — while the amount of food on their plates barely changed.

title: What Sparkling Water Really Does to Your Teeth
hook: Fizzy water is acidic, so people worry about their enamel. But soda's dip in mouth acidity was the deepest and longest — sparkling water's was brief, and never past the damage threshold.

title: Contraception Options
hook: There's no single 'best' contraception — only the one that fits your body, your life, and your plans. Knowing the main types helps you choose well.

title: The Mediterranean Diet May Work Through Tiny Mitochondrial Proteins
hook: The Mediterranean diet's heart and brain benefits may run through tiny proteins made inside your cells' mitochondria — and olive oil, fish, and legumes seem to boost them most.

title: Vaping and Cancer: The Evidence Is Mounting
hook: A major review concludes nicotine vapes are likely to cause lung and oral cancers — challenging the idea that vaping is a harmless alternative to smoking.

title: The Supplements Older Adults Actually Need
hook: For most older adults, the real question isn't which trendy supplement to take — it's whether you have a specific deficiency. B12, vitamin D, and often-overlooked protein are where it matters.

title: Finding a Healthy Weight
hook: BMI is a quick screen, not a verdict. A healthy weight is the range where your risk of disease stays low — and your waistline tells part of the story too.

title: The Brain Circuit That Ties Deep Sleep to Growth Hormone
hook: Scientists mapped the brain circuit linking deep sleep to growth hormone — a feedback loop that helps explain why poor sleep hits muscle repair, fat metabolism, and brain function at once.

title: Vitamin C and Cancer: The Route Changes Everything
hook: Linus Pauling was mocked for saying vitamin C fights cancer — because the trials used pills. Given intravenously it reaches concentrations that behave like a drug, not a vitamin.

title: Long-Term Melatonin Use and Heart Failure Risk
hook: Chronic-insomnia patients on long-term melatonin had roughly 90% higher heart failure risk over five years — an association, not proof, but a reason to stop assuming it is harmless.

title: A Protein That Shields the Brain From Alzheimer's Tau Damage
hook: Mice with extra SORLA, a protein already linked to Alzheimer's risk, developed less tau buildup, less brain atrophy, and healthier neural connections — pointing to a new drug target.

title: Your Brain Can Keep Improving — Even in Your 90s
hook: A three-year study of nearly 4,000 adults aged 19 to 94 found brain health can improve at any age, challenging the assumption that mental sharpness only declines with the years.

title: Exercise Doesn't Just Strengthen the Heart — It Rewires It
hook: Regular exercise doesn't only make the heart muscle stronger. New research finds it also rewires the nerves that control heart rhythm — a clue that could lead to more personalized treatment.

title: U.S. Measles Cases Hit a 35-Year High
hook: The CDC has confirmed 2,318 measles cases this year — the most since 1991, and the second record-breaking year in a row for a disease the U.S. once declared eliminated.

title: The Ozempic and Wegovy Mistake Sending Thousands to Poison Control
hook: Poison control calls about semaglutide (Ozempic and Wegovy) have soared — not from misuse, but from simple dosing mistakes that basic education could largely prevent.

title: Why Female Immunity Runs Hotter
hook: Women get autoimmune diseases like lupus far more often than men. Over 1,000 genetic switches behave differently in male and female immune cells — a stronger defense that can misfire.

title: Keeping Your Heart Healthy
hook: Most heart disease isn't bad luck — it's the sum of a few everyday habits. The American Heart Association distills them into eight that move the needle most.

title: What It Means When Prostate Cancer Spreads to Bone
hook: Joe Biden's cancer has reached his bones. An oncologist explains why bone is where prostate cancer usually goes — and why that isn't the end of the story.

title: Coffee May Fight Aging Through a Hidden Cellular Switch
hook: Scientists may have found why coffee tracks with healthier aging: its compounds activate NR4A1, a cellular switch that guards against stress and damage — and caffeine isn't the one doing it.

title: A Daily Fiber Supplement Eased Knee Arthritis Pain
hook: In a six-week trial, a spoonful of chicory-root fiber cut knee osteoarthritis pain about as well as physiotherapy — and people actually stuck with it. Only 3.6% dropped out, versus 21%.

title: Why Cutting Out All Sugar Can Backfire
hook: Cutting added sugar is good advice — but a mouse study suggests going to the extreme and eliminating it entirely may do more harm than good, pointing to balance over zero.

title: Heavy TV in Midlife, Smaller Brain Later
hook: A study of ~1,700 adults links lots of midlife TV to brain shrinkage decades on. The twist: sitting itself wasn't the villain — sitting at a mentally engaging job looked fine.

title: What the New Vaccine Executive Order Changes (For Now, Nothing)
hook: President Trump signed an executive order saying children should get fewer vaccines. The practical answer for parents this week: nothing has changed yet.
